message.content: {"0": {"original": "Wikipedia will go offline for 24 hours to protest U.S. anti-piracy laws, staring", "rephrased": "The online encyclopedia Wikipedia plans to shut down its global operations for 24 hours to demonstrate against proposed U.S. anti-piracy legislation, an action intended to highlight the potential threat these laws pose to the site's future.", "summary": "Wikipedia plans a 24-hour global shutdown to protest U.S. anti-piracy laws."}, "1": {"original": "Three administrators closed a key policy discussion to confirm the protest", "rephrased": "Three senior administrators within the Wikimedia Foundation officially confirmed the planned protest by closing a major policy debate on the site, signaling a decisive move to halt operations in opposition to the legislation.", "summary": "Wikimedia administrators confirmed the protest by closing a key policy discussion."}, "2": {"original": "479 users supported a U.S.-only blackout, while 591 backed a global one. During", "rephrased": "While a significant portion of the community favored a demonstration limited to the United States, a larger group of users advocated for a worldwide shutdown, with all participants instructed to contact their elected officials during the event.", "summary": "Community members are divided between supporting a U.S.-only or global blackout."}, "3": {"original": "The sites owned by Cheezburger Network are participating in the 24-hour global", "rephrased": "The Cheezburger Network, a major digital media company, has committed its various websites to joining the global 24-hour shutdown, aligning its operations with the broader coalition protesting the proposed U.S. anti-piracy laws.", "summary": "The Cheezburger Network is participating in the global blackout protest."}}
